tip: The verb pensar takes em, not de, and em + o becomes no: pensar no assunto = think about the matter.
With nunca before the verb, no second negative is needed: nunca esquecerei = I will never forget.
Fazer aniversário, literally to make a birthday, is the set phrase for having one: vai fazer aniversário.
Plain mudar means change; the reflexive se mudar means to relocate: vão se mudar para Curitiba.
Tinha plus a past participle is the pluperfect, an action done before another past moment: tinha cozinhado = had cooked.
Dar certo is the fixed phrase for to work out or turn out fine: vai dar tudo certo = it'll all work out.
To name the color something is painted, use de plus the color: pintado o quarto de branco = painted it white.
Com plus a noun often replaces an -mente adverb: com cuidado = carefully, literally with care.
Ligar meaning to phone someone takes para: tinha ligado para o médico = had called the doctor.
A gente means we but takes a singular verb: a gente vai, never a gente vão.
For a point in time the relative is em que, not bare que: o momento em que ele chegou = the moment when.
The preposition a plus o contracts to ao: iremos ao evento = we will go to the event.
In Brazilian Portuguese the pronoun goes before the infinitive: vou me inscrever, not vou inscrever-me.
After até, Portuguese uses an infinitive that names its own subject: até ela chegar = until she arrives.
For a future condition after quando, use the future subjunctive: quando for necessário = when it is necessary.
Será que opens a speculative question, like I wonder if or do you think: Será que ele vai aceitar?
After a preposition use a qual or o qual: por plus a qual becomes pela qual = along which.
Participar takes de, and de + o becomes do: participar do churrasco = take part in the barbecue.
Ter que plus an infinitive expresses obligation: vão ter que esperar = you'll have to wait.
Ir embora, not just ir, means to leave; embora is required: vão embora = they go away.
Onde means where and refers only to places: o museu onde vimos = the museum where we saw.
Tenho plus a participle isn't a one-time past; it means ongoing and repeated lately: tenho dormido mal = I've been sleeping badly.
For -ar verbs the imperfect subjunctive ends in -asse: falar becomes falasse, as in Se ela falasse = if she spoke.
